findings.title: super_admin role can be granted through membership/onboarding/bulk-invite APIs without the /users/:id/role guard
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/users.ts:406-420 — PATCH /users/:id/role explicitly refuses to assign the super_admin role unless the caller's profile has is_super_admin=true (the intended guard)
apps/api/src/validators/membership.ts:3-8 — updateMembershipSchema accepts any roleId uuid plus status, with no super_admin check
apps/api/src/routes/memberships.ts:95-104 — POST /memberships/invite inserts a membership with a caller-supplied roleId
apps/api/src/routes/memberships.ts:123-139 — PATCH /memberships/:id updates role_id/status for any membership in the caller's org scope (loadOwned checks the org, not the role)
apps/api/src/routes/bulk.ts:145-151 — bulk invite inserts memberships with a caller-supplied roleId under requireAdmin
apps/api/src/validators/organization.ts:42 + apps/api/src/routes/organizations.ts:77-125 — POST /organizations/onboard resolves an arbitrary adminRoleKey and inserts an approved membership with it

apps/api/src/lib/roles.ts:27,58-60 + apps/api/src/middleware/org-access.ts:37-60 — the super_admin role is the cross-tenant trust tier; middleware/admin.ts:49-58 only lets super_admin (not tenant admin) act while org-pinned
grep for triggers/guards on memberships role assignment in supabase/migrations — none found; service-role writes bypass RLS
findings.impact: A user holding the delegable users:manage permission, or any tenant admin, can create or edit a membership with role_id = super_admin (self, a colleague, or a new invited account). That moves the account into the cross-tenant trust tier: requireOrgAccess then grants access to every tenant as a platform admin (audited impersonation), and requireAdmin's org pinning from ADMIN-P1-001 no longer applies. The escalation path exists on three separate APIs while only one of four role-write paths is guarded.
findings.recommendation: Centralize role-assignment authorization in one helper (reject role key super_admin unless the caller profile is_super_admin) and use it from memberships invite/PATCH, bulk invite, organizations/onboard, and users/:id/role. Add regression tests for each path. Consider a DB trigger rejecting super_admin membership inserts/updates unless performed by a service context that carries an explicit super-admin assertion.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d. The /users/:id/role guard (users.ts:411-419) proves the intent; the membership and onboarding paths lack the same check.

findings.title: Worker monitoring checks are guard-then-fetch (DNS-rebinding TOCTOU); webhook path is pinned but uptime/website checks and SSL probe are not
evidence: apps/worker/src/tasks/module-tasks.ts:540,548-551 — uptime checks call assertSafeUrl() then plain fetch(check.url)
apps/worker/src/tasks/module-tasks.ts:590,602-605 — website monitors repeat the same guard-then-fetch pattern
apps/worker/src/tasks/module-tasks.ts:27-42 — fetchSslExpiry does a raw tls.connect({ host, port }) with no IP validation or pinning at all

apps/worker/src/tasks/webhook-dispatcher.ts:150 and apps/worker/src/tasks/webhook-retry.ts:122 — outbound webhooks already use pinnedFetch (the SEC-P2-002 fix), so the safe pattern exists in the same codebase
apps/worker/src/lib/ssrf-guard.ts:79-108 — the guard resolves DNS once; the subsequent fetch resolves again
findings.impact: A tenant admin who can create an uptime or website monitor (normal product feature) can supply a hostname that answers with a public IP for assertSafeUrl and a loopback/private/link-local address for the connection. The worker runs on the production droplet, so this is SSRF into Redis, Prometheus/Alertmanager, Caddy internals, or the DigitalOcean metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254). The webhook delivery path is fixed; monitoring is a residual of the same defect class.
findings.recommendation: Route uptime/website checks through pinnedFetch (or an equivalent pinned dispatcher) and pin the TLS socket in fetchSslExpiry to the validated address. Share a single SSRF/pinned-fetch module between apps/api and apps/worker so the guard cannot drift per call site.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d; SEC-P2-002 (webhook SSRF TOCTOU) is verified-fixed for webhooks, this is the monitoring residual.

findings.title: PII field encryption is additive: plaintext profile columns remain the source of truth and are still returned
evidence: supabase/migrations/5302135_profiles_encrypted_pii.sql:3-6,25-26 — the plaintext columns (full_name, email, phone, title) are intentionally kept as the source of truth for responses; encrypted_pii is a mirror
apps/api/src/routes/profiles.ts:159-175 — PATCH writes updateData.full_name/phone/title AND updateData.encrypted_pii
apps/api/src/routes/profiles.ts:61,108 — GET /profiles selects '*' so the raw encrypted_pii blob is returned to clients alongside the plaintext columns

apps/api/src/lib/field-encryption.ts:39-58 — encryptField fails closed in production (SEC-P1-001 fix), but nothing consumes decryptProfilePii on the read path (grep: only the lib and tests reference it)
findings.impact: The at-rest encryption control does not protect the PII it targets: a database read (backup, replica, leaked service key, SQL injection) still yields plaintext values in the same row. The encrypted copy adds schema/complexity and can drift from the plaintext columns without detection.
findings.recommendation: Complete the cutover the migration scaffold describes: read through decryptProfilePii, run scripts/backfill-profile-pii.mjs, then drop or null the plaintext columns (or replace them with a keyed hash for lookup), and add tests proving plaintext is not persisted. If the cutover is deferred, document it as a dated plan and stop advertising field-level encryption as effective at rest.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d. SEC-P1-001 (fail-closed encryption) is verified-fixed; this is the coverage gap of the control itself.

findings.title: Global role catalog is mutable by any org's roles:manage holder (roles are not org-scoped)
evidence: supabase/migrations/5302026_supabase_consolidated_fresh_bootstrap_20260529.corrected.v3.sql:161-168 — public.roles has no organization_id column (single global catalog)

apps/api/src/routes/roles.ts:269-271 — only the super_admin role's permissions are protected; every other role (including system roles used by other tenants) can have permissions granted or revoked
apps/api/src/middleware/permissions.ts:63-88 — with no resolvable org the caller's permission set is unioned across all of their orgs, so roles:manage in one tenant satisfies the gate
supabase/migrations/5302424_manage_actions.sql:22-29 — roles:manage is granted to admin/super_admin today but is delegable to custom roles
findings.impact: A delegated roles:manage holder (or any tenant admin, who bypasses the permission check) can rewrite the global authorization catalog for every tenant: grant themselves or a custom role extra permissions, or strip permissions from shared roles. Cross-tenant integrity of the RBAC model is not enforced at the API layer.
findings.recommendation: Gate global role/permission mutations on a platform-admin check (is_super_admin profile, matching resolveAdminTenantScope's allTenants rule) or make custom roles organization-scoped. Audit-log the actor's org context for every catalog mutation.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d; related to ACM-P2-004 (action mismatch) but a distinct cross-tenant integrity gap.

findings.title: API-key scopes are stored but never enforced; keys act with the creating user's full permissions and always bypass RLS

apps/api/src/middleware/auth.ts:70-82 — they are attached to req.apiKey.permissions, but middleware/permissions.ts never reads req.apiKey (grep 'req.apiKey' finds only auth.ts)

findings.recommendation: Enforce req.apiKey.permissions in requirePermission (intersect with resolved permissions) or drop the column and document that keys inherit the creator's permissions. Add permissions to the create schema + admin UI if scoping is intended. Require a permission on GET /api-keys. Document the RLS-bypass for API keys.

findings.title: Sign-up confirmation redirect is built from the caller-controlled Host header and targets a non-existent API route
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts:182 — emailRedirectTo: `${req.protocol}://${req.get('host')}/auth/callback` (Host header is caller-controlled)
apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts:33-57 — forgot-password by contrast resolves a trusted origin via resolveTrustedRedirectOrigin (CHAIN-P1-002 fix)
apps/api/src/app.ts:174 — the API only serves POST /api/v1/auth/callback; there is no GET /auth/callback on the API origin
apps/web/app/auth/callback/route.ts:8 — the web callback lives at /auth/callback on the web origin
supabase/config.toml.production.example:29-34 — additional_redirect_urls allowlists only portal/auth callback URLs, so Supabase is expected to fall back to site_url
findings.impact: A caller-controlled host is echoed into a Supabase confirmation email redirect. Supabase's redirect allowlist is the only thing preventing the link from pointing at an attacker host (phishing/redirect, and token/code delivery to a third party if the allowlist is loosened). The API-origin path is also wrong for the real web callback, so the flow depends entirely on Supabase's fallback.
findings.recommendation: Build emailRedirectTo from APP_BASE_URL (or resolveTrustedRedirectOrigin) plus the web callback path, mirroring the forgot-password fix; add a regression test asserting a spoofed Host cannot influence the redirect.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d. Exploitability depends on the Supabase project's redirect allowlist (not verifiable from the repo).

## Executive Summary

The security posture is materially stronger than the previous full run's baseline: field encryption fails closed, the reset redirect is no longer caller-controlled, webhook dispatch and webhook test calls use a DNS-pinned fetch, the anon DML blanket grant is gone, `/health` no longer leaks provider state, RLS predicate hygiene has a CI guard, and API keys actually authenticate. The org-pinned `requireAdmin` + `resolveAdminTenantScope` combination closes the tenant-admin cross-tenant read path, and the audit/impersonation trail is reviewable by genuine platform admins only.

The most important **new** risk is a privilege-escalation gap in role assignment: `PATCH /memberships/:id`, `POST /memberships/invite`, `POST /bulk/invite` and `POST /organizations/onboard` all accept a caller-chosen role (id/key) without the `super_admin` guard that `/users/:id/role` enforces. A user with the delegable `users:manage` permission (or any tenant admin) can mint a `super_admin` membership and move into the cross-tenant trust tier that `ADMIN-P1-001` pinning relies on.

Secondary themes: the PII encryption control is additive (plaintext stays authoritative), the worker's monitoring fetches retain the DNS-rebinding TOCTOU fixed for webhooks, API-key scopes are stored but ignored, the global RBAC catalog is mutable by an org-scoped `roles:manage`, and MFA remains opt-in with a `false` deployed default.

Recommended next actions: fix the role-assignment guard this week (one shared helper + tests); route monitoring through `pinnedFetch`; decide the PII cutover; enforce or drop API-key scopes; and make admin accounts require aal2.

- Evidence: `middleware/auth.ts:46-181`, `lib/mfa.ts`, `routes/auth.ts:404-730`, `apps/web/lib/auth/auth-actions.ts`.
- What it does: verifies HS256 JWTs against a comma-separated secret list, falls back to Supabase `getUser` (5 s timeout), then applies MFA step-up when `MFA_ENFORCEMENT_ENABLED` is true and the user has a verified TOTP factor.
- Missing controls: MFA default off; SSE revalidation (`routes/notifications.ts:89`) verifies without `algorithms` pinning; sign-up `emailRedirectTo` uses the request Host.
- Risks: admin sessions password-only by default (new finding); Host echo in confirmation email (new finding).

### Item: Authorization middleware and tenant scoping

- Evidence: `middleware/admin.ts:22-64`, `middleware/org-access.ts:20-325`, `middleware/permissions.ts:54-93`, `lib/admin-scope.ts`, `lib/tenant.ts`, `lib/roles.ts`.
- What it does: pins admin checks to the resolved org unless the caller holds `super_admin`; only `admin`/`super_admin` cross tenants; `assertBodyOrgMatches` rejects body/query org mismatches; `loadOwned`/`assertResourceOrg` enforce row ownership.
- Missing controls: role-assignment paths do not validate `super_admin`; `roles` catalog mutations are not platform-gated.
- Risks: privilege escalation to the cross-tenant tier (new P1); cross-tenant RBAC catalog mutation (new P2).

### Item: API keys

- Evidence: `middleware/api-key.ts`, `middleware/auth.ts:67-88`, `routes/api-keys.ts`, `supabase/migrations/5302042_api_keys.sql`.
- What it does: prefix lookup + SHA-256 timing-safe compare, active/expiry checks, org pinning, best-effort `last_used_at`.
- Missing controls: stored `permissions` are never enforced; create API cannot set them; GET list has no permission gate; RLS never applies (no `req.userJwt`).
- Risks: scoped keys silently over-privileged; RLS rollout blind spot (new finding).

### Item: Webhooks and SSRF

- Evidence: `routes/webhooks.ts`, `lib/webhook-signature.ts`, `lib/pinned-fetch.ts`, `apps/worker/src/tasks/{webhook-dispatcher,webhook-retry,module-tasks}.ts`.

### Finding: super_admin role can be granted through membership/onboarding/bulk-invite APIs without the /users/:id/role guard

- Severity: P1
- Confidence: High
- Area: SEC
- Evidence:
  - `apps/api/src/routes/users.ts:406-420` — the only path with the explicit `super_admin` assignment guard
  - `apps/api/src/validators/membership.ts:3-8`; `apps/api/src/routes/memberships.ts:95-104,123-139` — invite/PATCH accept any `roleId`
  - `apps/api/src/routes/bulk.ts:145-151`; `apps/api/src/validators/organization.ts:42`; `apps/api/src/routes/organizations.ts:77-125` — bulk invite and onboarding accept any role id/key
  - `apps/api/src/lib/roles.ts:27`; `apps/api/src/middleware/org-access.ts:37-60`; `apps/api/src/middleware/admin.ts:49-58` — `super_admin` is the cross-tenant, unpinned tier
- What is happening: role assignment is validated on one route only; the other three accept the caller's role choice, including `super_admin`.
- Why it matters: a delegable `users:manage` holder or tenant admin can promote any account (or themselves) into the trust tier that `ADMIN-P1-001` org pinning depends on.
- Security impact: cross-tenant read/write on every `requireOrgAccess`/`requireAdmin` surface, audited only as impersonation.
- Recommended fix: one shared `assertRoleAssignable(req, roleKey/roleId)` helper used by all four paths; DB trigger as backstop.
- Suggested validation: integration tests per path asserting a non-super-admin caller receives 403 when assigning `super_admin`.
- Owner suggestion: API principal engineer / security. Effort: M. Status: open.

### Finding: Worker monitoring checks are guard-then-fetch (DNS-rebinding TOCTOU)

- Severity: P2
- Confidence: High
- Evidence: `apps/worker/src/tasks/module-tasks.ts:540,548-551,590,602-605`; `fetchSslExpiry` at `:27-42`; contrast `apps/worker/src/tasks/webhook-dispatcher.ts:150` and `apps/worker/src/tasks/webhook-retry.ts:122` (pinnedFetch)
- What is happening: uptime/website monitor URLs are DNS-validated once and then fetched again; the SSL probe does a raw `tls.connect`.
- Why it matters: a tenant admin (monitor creation is a normal feature) can point a rebinding hostname at loopback/private addresses on the worker host.
- Security impact: SSRF into Redis/Prometheus/metadata from the production droplet.
- Recommended fix: use `pinnedFetch` for checks and pin the TLS socket; share the guard module between api/worker.
- Suggested validation: unit test with a resolver that returns a public address then a loopback address; assert the fetch is blocked.
- Owner suggestion: API/worker platform engineer. Effort: S–M. Status: open.

### Finding: PII field encryption is additive: plaintext profile columns remain the source of truth

- Severity: P2
- Confidence: High
- Evidence: `supabase/migrations/5302135_profiles_encrypted_pii.sql:3-6,25-26`; `apps/api/src/routes/profiles.ts:159-175` (writes both), `:61,108` (selects `*`); `lib/profile-pii.ts` decrypt helper unused on reads
- What is happening: every profile write stores an encrypted mirror next to unchanged plaintext columns.
- Why it matters: a DB read still yields plaintext; the control does not protect against the threat it targets.
- Recommended fix: decrypt on read, run the backfill, drop/blank plaintext; or document a dated cutover and stop advertising at-rest encryption.
- Suggested validation: test that a profile write leaves no plaintext in `full_name/email/phone/title` after cutover.
- Owner suggestion: API/backend + data governance. Effort: M–L. Status: open.
